newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says its most famous resort isn't safe.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says its most famous resort isn't safe.

text.p: The Philippines' most famous resort, Boracay island, is not safe for swimming and it could take 10 years to remove the human waste that has leaked into the water, the country's Environment Secretary said on Monday.
"It's already a disaster area and we are not encouraging people to bathe," Victor Ramos told a news conference.
"No area in the island is safe from coliform contamination."

Its sparkling white sand and clear blue sea have made the island one of the most popular tourist destinations in the Philippines with hotels sprouting faster than a rudimentary sewerage system can cope.
Ramos said water samples taken by his staff indicated Boracay was contaminated by high levels of coliform bacteria which can cause diarrhoea, typhoid and skin diseases.
Tourism Secretary Mina Gabor immediately contested Ramos' comments, saying Ramos had previously told her the tests conducted in the central Philippines island were inconclusive.
More tests must be taken in different parts of Boracay for at least a year to verify the initial study conducted for three months last year, she quoted Ramos as saying.
Philippine tourism officials said several tourists cancelled visits to the island after local newspapers reported earlier this month results of the study done by the Environment department.

"All the beautiful things and attributes written about Boracay as the world's best beach have diminished in meaning if articles like this go uncorrected," Edwin Trompeta, regional director of the Tourism department, said in a letter to Gabor.
